Welcome to Middle Park Primary School
Learn together, grow together
Welcome to Middle Park Primary School
Middle Park is a happy and successful community school which caters for children aged 3-11.
We have a dynamic staff team who are committed to all our learners. We pride ourselves on offering an enriching curriculum that is broad, balanced and inclusive.
Our ‘exciting and inclusive ‘ Early Years provision offers our youngest children a fantastic start on their learning journey. You can talk to us about how we can offer the 30-hour entitlement.
Please don’t hesitate to contact us if you have any questions or queries.
Middle Park Primary School is a learning community, committed to the education of the whole child. We are always seeking new and creative ways of engaging children in learning experiences that motivate them and support them to develop a life long love of learning.
Our fundamental school vision is that every single child achieves to their full potential. We know that this is best achieved through high quality teaching that is engaging, innovative and personalised to the needs of every child.
We highly value the voice of our children and continually develop structures and systems which ensure they always have an input into all decisions which affect their school. We also enjoy a strong relationship with our parents and carers and are very proud of our community feel. All stakeholders are encouraged to become as involved in school life as they can and their comments and suggestions are always welcomed.
We value learning experiences both inside and outside. We organise a consistent annual programme of educational visits and two residential school journeys. We have five qualified Forest School leaders who support children from Nursery to Year 1 in learning in an outdoor setting.
We are very proud of our school and are continually striving to be the very best we can be for our children and families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolBritish Values - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
School Information: British Values at Middle Park
At Middle Park Primary School we uphold and teach pupils about British Values. The Department for Education states that there is a need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy and these values were reiterated by the Prime Minister in 2014. At Middle Park Primary School we promote and teach the following values through our Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural education which permeates through our curriculum. In particular, the following British values are taught and discussed with pupils:
Tolerance of Faiths and Belief
This is achieved through enhancing pupils’ understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience diversity. Assemblies and discussions involving prejudices and prejudice-based bullying have been followed and supported by learning in RE and PSHE.
Members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school. We regularly hold whole-school assemblies to celebrate and learn about the numerous religious festivals that happen throughout the school year. We harness cultural links in our classes and often reach out into the community to support our teaching.
At Middle Park Primary School we pride ourselves on our positive relationships. We treat each other with mutual respect and work in a climate where openness, trust and inclusion lay the foundations for future life.
Our school values underpin all aspects of school life and give staff and children the opportunity to discuss and reflect on the values in life that they believe in. It is our values that determine our thinking and behaviour and the way in which we interpret the world around us. Learning and effort are highly respected and the whole school is focused on developing an intrinsic sense of worth and achievement.
We aim to help children learn the art of reflection and questioning. We teach them to be understanding of others and solution focussed rather than judging others and getting cross. By the time children leave Middle Park Primary School, they understand that values are important if people in our society are going to live happily together.
Freedom and Democracy
Democracy is core to our School Ethos. Children have the opportunity to have their voices heard through our School Council and Pupil questionnaires. Elections for School Council representatives are undertaken in each class.
We encourage children to be leaders throughout the school and we have a number of activities and responsibilities that are undertaken by the children. For example, pupils from Key Stage 2 are prefects and play leaders at lunch and play times they are responsible for encouraging all children to take part at playtime by inviting them into games.
Children are always able to voice their opinions and we foster an environment where children are safe to disagree with each other, through the development of speaking and listening skills.
Within school, children are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. They develop vocabulary to enter into a dialogue with others in their decision making.
As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safely through the provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Children are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise this safely. An example of this is through our E-Safety and PSHE lessons. Pupils are given the freedom to make choices through challenge, recording learning and participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities.
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country are consistently reinforced. This is through our expectations throughout every school day, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies.
At Middle Park Primary School we ensure that children are acutely aware of their responsibilities. Children develop a thorough understanding of personal responsibility and develop independence in managing relationships and behaviour.
Each class works together to create a set of class rules that they feel are appropriate for them. Children are involved in the decision making and the reasons why these rules are important.
Children are taught the value and reasons behind laws and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service etc. are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce this message.

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolPlay Leaders - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Play Leaders
Some of Year Five and Year Six children have been trained by Diane as play-leaders to help our children play together, learn new games and resolve any problems. Look out for their special t-shirts in the playground.
Our school Play Leader Scheme starts in the upper juniors. At the beginning of the year, these children can apply for the job, and if successful they will receive training and become one of our Play Leaders. The job of a Play Leader is to encourage younger children to be active, and to play constructive games together. Each Play Leader will be on duty once a week. They take an early lunch, don their red or green t-shirt and under the watchful eye of the Playground Manager, spend that lunchtime setting out equipment, and organising various games.
They also organise and run a Sports Day for the Foundation Stage, as well as helping out the Infants at their Sports Day.
The scheme works very well developing the leadership skills of the older children whilst ensuring the younger children are active and learning to play well together.

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolReporting to parents and carers - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Reporting to parents and carers
Parents and Carers receive a written report of their pupils’ achievements at the end of the academic year. This report summarises progress made throughout the year and builds on discussions from Academic Tutoring Days.
Academic Tutoring Days (ATD)
These are important formal meetings that happen twice a year for each pupil and provide an opportunity for parents and carers to discuss their child’s progress and achievements.
During Academic Tutoring days children still come into school as usual. Parents and carers are given an appointment during the day to meet with the class teacher. Children will join parents/carers to talk about their progress and targets. Letters will be sent out prior to academic tutoring days, we aim to give as much notice as possible.
Parents are encouraged and welcomed to make additional appointments with the class teacher throughout the year to discuss any concerns.
Reporting to Parents/Carers letter July 2024
This is set by the government tells us what we have to teach at different stages of schooling. It sets out the subjects pupils must be taught. Schools decide the best way to deliver the curriculum taking into account the needs of pupils.
Teachers make continual assessments of pupils’ understanding and provide feedback to help them improve.
Standard Assessment Tests. Currently, SATs are compulsory in Year 2 and Year 6. Year 6 SATs papers are sent away and marked externally, while Year 2 SATs inform teacher assessment. Assessments in both Year 2 and Year 6 are moderated by the Local Authority.
Moderation is a way of checking that our assessments are accurate. Sometimes we moderate together in school, sometimes we get together with other schools to moderate, and sometimes the Local Authority will come in to school to moderate our results.
PUPIL PROGRESS MEETINGS
Are meetings we hold in school where senior staff and teachers work together to check the accuracy of assessments. We aim to ensure that we are doing everything possible to support individual children in achieving their full potential.
Pupils are ‘tracked’ in various ways to ensure that progress is assured and that no child is ever over-looked. Teachers track their own class in reading, writing and maths. Subject Leaders track progress in their subjects, and the Senior Leadership Team analyse attainment in classes, year groups and key stages.
An intervention is an action taken in school to support a child in their progression. We currently run various invention programmes in reading, writing and maths as well as our Inclusion Team who support children in overcoming any barriers to learning.

SEND Local Offer/Information Report
For children and young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities All Greenwich maintained schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of pupils with Special Educational Needs and/or disabilities, and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all pupils, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school.
All schools are supported to be as inclusive as possible, with the needs of pupils with a Special Educational Need/s being met in a mainstream setting wherever possible, where families want this to happen. Nearly all children with Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) go to a ‘mainstream’ school.
At Middle Park Primary School we recognise that many children may need some extra help or support at some time during their journey through school. We feel it is essential to the child’s development that children who do have a Special Educational Need or Disability (SEND) are identified as early as possible. This is known as early intervention and makes sure they get the help they need. This School offer should be looked at together with:
The Royal Borough of Greenwich Local Offer for children and young people with SEND, which can be accessed Through the Royal Borough Of Greenwich Website.
The school Bullying Prevention Policy, which can be accessed under our Policies on the website.
The school accessibility plan, which can be accessed under our Policies on the website.
Middle Park Primary School – Our vision
Our vision is to ensure that every Middle Park child experiences success in their learning and achieves at the highest possible standard regardless of their need. We aspire to ensure all children are able to fully participate effectively in their learning and contribute to whole school life. Definition of Special Educational Needs and Disability The definition given in the 2014 ‘ Special educational needs and disability code of practice: 0 to 25 years’ stated:
A child or young person has SEN if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for him or her. A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty or disability if he or she,
Who are the best people to talk to in at Middle Park Primary School about my child’s difficulties with learning/Special Educational Needs/Disability (SEND)? How can I talk to them about my child if I need to?
The Class Teachers
If you have any concerns or would just like to come and have a chat about your child and their needs you are always very welcome to arrange a meeting with their class teacher. Sometimes after talking to the teacher, who spends every day with your child, can help to clarify and find ways to support your child in a specific area of need.
Responsible for:
Ensuring that the school’s SEND Policy is followed in their classroom and for all the pupils they teach with any SEND.
Teachers can be contacted by phoning the school number: 0208 850 8747
Teaching Assistants (TAs) may be allocated to some pupils with SEN and or disabilities) A Teaching Assistant (TA) may be allocated to a pupil with exceptional special educational needs and/or disabilities and whilst they take a very valuable role in your child’s education we would prefer that questions regarding your child’s learning and progress, are directed to class teachers or SENCo. Of course, as a school we welcome daily dialogue between parents and TAs on how a child’s day has been and we do actively encourage this continued feedback
The Special Educational Needs Coordinator: Claire Evans KS1/KS2 Emma McCarron EYFS
If you still have concerns you are also very welcome to come and speak to the school SENCo’s (Special Educational Needs Coordinator), Claire Evans or Emma McCarron. They will discuss strategies and processes that are available depending on the child’s individual need.
Responsible for:
Contacted by email – cevans@middlepark.greenwich.sch.uk or telephone 0208 8508747
The Deputy Head : Carrie Hogger
Carrie Hogger is responsible for inclusion and will be happy to discuss any further concerns.
Headteacher – Donna Adkinson
Responsible for:
She must make sure that the Governing Body is kept up to date about any issues in the school relating to SEND.
Contacted by email – headteacher@middlepark.greenwich.sch.uk or telephone 0208 850 8747
SEND Governor
Responsible for:
Children in school will get support that is specific to their individual needs. This may be all provided by the class teacher or may involve:
How could my child get help at Middle Park Primary School?
The Class Teacher will ensure Quality First Teaching in the classroom.
This will mean that:
Specific small group work
It may be that a pupil may benefit from working in a small group to access specific learning. This group, often called an intervention group, may be run in the classroom or outside the classroom and led by a specialist teacher, class teacher or Teaching Assistant under the guidance of the SENCo and/or teacher. This will mean that:
Your child may take part in group sessions targets to help them make progress
A teacher or Teaching Assistant (TA) may run small group sessions.
This level of support is available for any child who has specific gaps in their understanding of a subject/area of learning.
Specialist groups run by outside agencies e.g Speech and Language therapy OR Occupational therapy groups AND/OR individual support for your child (20 hours and below in school)
Your child’s teacher or SENCo may identify them as needing some extra specialist support in school from a professional outside school.
This may be from:
Local Authority central services such as ASD (Autistic Spectrum Disorder) Outreach Team or Sensory Service ( for students with hearing or visual need)
Outside agencies such as the Speech and Language Therapy (SALT) Service
For your child this would mean:
Your child has been identified (by the class teacher, SENDCo or you will have raised concerns), as needing more specialist assessment and input in addition to quality first teaching or intervention groups
Referrals made to outside agencies will be done after discussion with you and your signed consent.
Recommendations may include:
Making changes to the way your child is supported in class e.g. some individual support or changing some aspects of teaching to support them better
Support to set targets which will include their specific professional expertise
Your child’s involvement in a group run by school staff under the guidance of the outside professional e.g. a social skills group, speech and language/social communication group or sensory circuit
A group or individual work with an outside professional
Suggested about equipment and resources that will either be provided by the agency or by the school to support your child in their learning
The school may suggest that your child needs some agreed individual support or group support in school. They will tell you how the support will be used and what strategies will be put in place.
This type of support is available for pupils with specific barrier to learning that cannot be overcome through Quality First Teaching
Specified individual support for your child of more than 20 hours in school EHCP Support
This is usually provided through an Educational, Health and Care Plan(EHCP). This means your child would have been identified by the class teacher/SENCo as needing a particularly high level of individual and small group teaching or other support (more than 20 hrs a week) Which cannot be provided from the resources already delegated to the school.
Usually, if your child requires this high level of support they may also need specialist support from a professional outside the school.
This may include:
Local Authority central services as the ASD Outreach Team or Sensory Service as well as Speech and Language (SALT) Service, Occupational Therapy Service, Physiotherapy and/or CAMHS (Child and Adolescent Mental Health services)
For your child would mean:
The school (or you) can request that the Local Authority carry out a statutory assessment of your child’s needs.
This is a legal process and you can find more details about this in the Local Authority (LA) based Local Offer by visiting the Royal Borough of Greenwich website
www.royalgreenwich.gov.uk
After the school has submitted all the reports, including information from you and other agencies involved e.g. doctors and other health services, the Local Authority will decide if your child’s needs are severe, complex and lifelong and that they need more than 20 hours of support in school to make good progress. If this is the case they will write an Educational Health Care Plan. If this is not the case, they will ask the school to continue to ensure a plan is in place so that your child makes as much progress as possible
The EHC plan will outline the banding allocation of individual/small group support your child will receive from the LA and how the support should be used and what strategies must be put in place. It will also have outcomes for your child to work towards
SEN support
Some of the children accessing intervention groups may be at the stage of the SEND Code of Practice called School SEN Support, which means they have been identified by class teacher as needing some extra support in school, after putting strategies in place at class level. For your child this would mean:
Addional support available:
How will we support your child with identified special needs starting at school?
We will first invite you to visit the school with your child to have a look around and speak to staff If other professionals are involved, we will share strategies used, and ensure provision is put in place before your child starts if needed. We may suggest adaptations to the settling in period to help your child to settle more easily.
How can you let the school know you are concerned about your child’s progress in school?
If you have concerns about your child’s progress please initially speak to your child’s class teacher If you are not happy that the concerns are being managed and your child is still not making progress then you should speak to the SENCo (Claire Evans/Emma McCarron) or Deputy Head (Carrie Hogger) If you are still not happy you can speak to the school SEND Governor.
How will the school let me know if they have any concerns about my child’s learning in school?
When a teacher or a parent has raised concerns about your child’s progress, and targeted teaching has not met the child’s needs, the teacher will raise this with the SENCo. There are pupil progress meetings every term between each class teacher and a senior staff member in the school to ensure all children are making good progress. This is another way your child may be identified as not making as much progress as expected.
If your child is then identified as not making progress the school will make a decision about whether to monitor this or set up an intervention group and will inform you. If your child is still not making expected progress the school will discuss with you:
We have Academic Tutoring Days during the year to give parents and teachers an opportunity to discuss progress and learning on an individual basis.
How is extra support allocated to children and how do they move between the different levels?
The school budget, received from Greenwich LA, includes money for supporting children with SEND. The Head Teacher decides on the budget for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in consultation with the school governors, on the basis of needs in the school. The Head Teacher and the SENCO discuss all the information they have about SEND in the school, including:
◦ the children getting extra support already
◦ the children needing extra support
◦ the children who have been identified as not making as much progress as would be expected and decide what resources/training and support is needed. All resources/training and support are reviewed regularly and changes made as needed.
Who are the other people providing services to children with SEND in Middle Park Primary School?
To support children with Special Educational Needs we sometimes work with other professionals who have expertise in specific areas. If this is the case we would always discuss this with the parents.
Outside Agencies we work alongside:
◦ Family Liaison officer
◦ Additional Speech and Language Therapy input to provide a higher level of service to the school
◦ Additional Educational Psychology input to provide a higher level of service to the school
◦ CAMHS B : Paid for centrally by the Local Authority but delivered in school:
Autism Outreach Service
Educational Psychology
Service Sensory Service for children with visual or hearing needs
STEPS (Assessment, advice and resources for children with literacy or numeracy difficulties including Dyslexia
Speech and Language Therapy (provided by Health but paid for by the Local Authority).
Occupational Therapy
Physiotherapy Professional training for school staff to deliver medical interventions
Waterside Behaviour service
Parent Partnership Service (to support families through the SEN processes and procedures).
Please find out more information from each of these agencies on the Royal borough of Greenwich Local Offer:
http://familiesinformation.royalgreenwich.gov.uk/kb5/greenwich/fsd/results.page
Any concerns you may have
How are adults in school helped to work with children with SEND and what training do they have?
The SENCo’s job is to support the class teacher in planning for children with SEND. The school has a School Development Plan, including identified training needs for all staff to improve the teaching and learning of children, including those with SEND. pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolHome learning - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Home learning
We aim to promote carefully balanced home learning opportunities for pupils.
Home learning is most effective when completed in a supportive and secure environment. It is important to set aside time so the learning is productive. We have found pupils make better progress when they are helped with their home learning, particularly reading.
All pupils have books for home learning and reading records. Parents are encouraged to add comments in reading records. Workbooks and reading records should be returned to school regularly.
The amount of home learning is regularly monitored and class teachers are always happy to discuss activities and give advice. Occasionally pupils will be encouraged to visit a local place or an event linked to learning in school.
We view family time as important and class teachers consider the length of time needed to complete tasks. Our pupils learn in different ways and any concerns should be raised with the class teacher.
The most important aspect of home learning is reading. This can be your child reading to you or you reading to your child. Please make undisturbed time for this every day. Enjoy reading together! Reading helps our pupils expand their minds and will increase general knowledge.
Each year group will explain home learning expectations in more detail on their termly newsletters.
In the event of a school closure
Pupils will be provided with learning should school need to close. An email will be sent to parents from their class teacher containing details of the learning to take place. Daily timings and links to live lessons will also be provided.

SMSC is about the values pupils are encouraged to hold and their attitude towards learning, knowledge and society. At Middle Park Primary School we believe that the social, moral, spiritual and cultural development of our children is fundamental in preparing them for society. During their time at Middle Park Primary School, we encourage children to:

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolMathematics - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
Our Maths curriculum enables children to have the opportunity to explore number, shape and space and measures through games, puzzles and investigations. We encourage children to look for patterns and justify their understanding. Teachers ensure that the children secure mathematical knowledge at each stage, building up a body of knowledge, methods, processes, concepts and uses for mathematics as they progress through school. Maths teaches the children beneficial life skills that can be used in the wider world such as leadership, creativity, problem-solving, collaboration and logical thinking.
Formal written calculations and mental calculations are taught throughout the school. We aim to develop a repertoire of methods that children are able to select from when faced with problem solving activities. Mathematics is taught using a variety of different strategies to enable children to become fluent in their mathematical knowledge. It also enables the children to give reasons and demonstrate their knowledge in practical ways, using mathematical vocabulary to explain their predictions and ideas, as well as using this knowledge to solve problems.
Our aim is to ensure children think and act as mathematicians through effective communication of their mathematical understanding. At Middle Park children learn all about the ever-changing world around them in readiness and preparation for a career beyond school. Mathematics is linked across the wider curriculum to range of subjects and forms part of our STEM learning. (Science, technology, engineering and maths) Providing these links gives our children a holistic STEM learning experience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolPSHE - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
PSHE
Personal, Social, Health and Citizenship Education
PSHCE is immersed in the daily life of the school through behaviour at break-times, assemblies and healthy eating at lunch time. PSCHE is taught explicitly and through other subjects. Middle Park has an active school council who meet regularly. Pupil voice is valued at Middle Park and pupils’ opinions are sought when introducing a new initiative or evaluating existing one. Children are encouraged to talk about their learning and aspirations for their future development.
Teaching includes drug awareness and sex and relationships education. These are taught in a sensitive way and help to prepare children for physical and emotional changes as they move into adulthood.
Middle Park takes part in many initiatives to support learning in this subject. These include an extensive school travel plan, challenging stereotypes and special events such as International Day and ‘Random Acts of Kindness’ week.

pageCache.pageTitle: Middle Park Primary SchoolForeign languages - Middle Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Foreign languages
At Middle Park, learning the French language provides a valuable educational, social and cultural experience for our pupils. It helps them to develop communication skills including key skills of speaking, listening and writing and extends their knowledge of how language works. Learning another language gives children a new perspective on the world, encouraging them to understand their own cultures and those of others.
Our French lessons enthuse, engage and motivate pupils to foster their curiosity and enthusiasm for the learning. A multi-sensory and kinaesthetic approach to teaching is used in the delivery of the subject, with an emphasis on the use of practical activities that are dynamic, inspirational and fun. We try to make lessons as enjoyable as possible so that the children develop a positive attitude to the learning of French. Children’s confidence is increased by praise for any contribution they make, however tentative.
At Middle Park, we address the Primary National Curriculum for Modern Foreign Languages through making the learning of a new language fun and exciting using themed blocks of work. The aims and objectives of learning a foreign language in Middle Park School are to;

On this page you will find details and photographs of the members of our Governing Body. You will see that they come from various backgrounds and have a variety of expertise to offer the school.

Co-Opted Governors
Carol Ladbrook(Chair of Governors) Co-Opted Governor Term of Office ends November 2029
I am Carol Ladbrook and I am the Chair of Governors. I became a parent governor at Middle Park Primary School when my son, Robert, was in year 3 – he’s now 31 and National Editor for two motorsport publications! I was appointed as a co-opted governor
A Message from the Chair of Governors
We have a very committed and hard-working governing body at Middle Park Primary School that works in partnership with the Headteacher and staff to ensure the school is successful and the pupils achieve high standards in a safe and caring environment. The GB membership includes staff governors, parent governors, our local ward councillor who is nominated by the Local Authority and co-opted governors who are appointed by the GB. Co-opted governors are representatives from the local community who bring a range of different skills and interests to the GB.
The Governing Body meets once each term and is responsible for:
In order to fulfil these duties, we have two main committees:
We also have a Pay Committee and a Pay Appeals Committee.
I am very proud to be associated with the school for so many years and to work with knowledgeable and dedicated staff and great fellow governors. I am extremely proud of Middle Park Primary School – we have dedicated and skilled staff, supportive parents and wonderfully enthusiastic and creative children.
Carol LadbrookChair of Governors
Tony Hutchings(Vice Chair+Chair of Business Committee) Co-Opted Governor Term of Office Ends June 2029
I have been a co-opted governor at Middle Park School since November 2014.
As a former pupil of Middle Park I know that the education children receive at primary school is critical to them fulfilling their full capability. I wanted to become a school governor at Middle Park to ensure that it continues to offer the life chances that it gave me all those years ago.
I attend all the main governing body meetings and play an active role on the business committee and the learning and achievement committee.
I bring a range of senior management and leadership skills to the governing body from almost 30 years working in various roles within BT.
As a Governor I attend different meetings and events in school and regularly undertake specific governor training to make sure I can make a positive contribution to the success of the school. I have particularly enjoyed seeing the engagement of the children in school and the variety of external opportunities they have to grow as individuals.
My outside interests include: cycling, golf, walking and bowls.
Norma Spruce(Vice Chair Business Committee +SCR) Co-Opted Governor Term of Office Ends May 2029
I was introduced to Middle Park over 20 years ago when working for Alcatel-Lucent in Greenwich. I was appointed as a co-opted governor and joined the business committee where I am still an active member using my business experience and skills to oversee the financial performance of the school and ensuring that its money is well spent. This involves reviewing plans for staffing, building projects, learning initiatives and monitoring expenditure. We are very fortunate at MPPS to have robust and clear financial management and monitoring that underpins the school plans for inclusion and enrichment for its children.
I have always had an interest in education for all and it is inspiring to see the commitment of teaching and support staff to ensure that every child achieves their potential. I live in Eltham and it is a privilege to be part of the local community and to contribute to the support and success of MPPS.
As well as committee and governing body meetings, I visit the school and attend various sports and academic events, where I can meet teachers, parents, and children.
Now retired, I am fully committed to being a wise woman and adventurer, which means I have time to enjoy lots of leisure activities including foreign travel, sport, urban farming on my allotment, learning to play the piano and making the most of London’s theatres and art galleries. It also means that I have time to attend governor-training courses and to keep up to date with latest developments in local and national education matters that may impact on the running of school.
Carla Marques(Vice Chair +SEN/Safeguarding) Co-Opted Governor Term of Office Ends June 2029
I am now a Co-opted Governor, having previously been a Parent Governor for nearly 4 years.
I have worked with kids and teenagers for 22 years. As a mother of 2 children and a professional in the education area, I can balance both personal and professional experience and knowledge to be a school critical friend. I am really passionate about Middle Park Primary School and do my best to be a very active governor. I am member of 4 committees: Business, Learning and Achievement, Pay and Performance Management.
Brian DonnelleyCo-Opted Governor Term of Office Ends June 2029
I am Brian Donnelley and I have worked at the school as the Premises Manager for the past 21 years. I am currently a staff governor but have also been a parent governor when my children were at Middle Park. They both had an excellent time at the school and left fully prepared for their next stage at Eltham Green (now Harris Academy)
I have lived and worked in Eltham all my life and love the area. In my spare time I love to walk my 2 rescue dogs and often go on walks with the Bull Terrier rescue group.
Co-Opted Governor Term of office ends June 2028
I have been a parent at Middle Park primary school for the past five years. I have four beautiful children and seeing them run into the school gates every morning excited to see their amazing teachers & learn is what prompted me to get more involved. I wanted to be part of their school journey and contribute to what is already such a wonderful school, the bond between the parents & staff members as parents drop their children for 6 hours knowing they are in great hands is what also really stood out for me. The trust that is there and the sense of community where everyone matters and work together to create the best environment for both the children and staff so that everyone can benefit greatly in their daily life at Middle Park.
I am currently at university studying English Language & English Language teaching. I was very fortunate to have encountered some of the best teacher’s year in and year out who have gone above and beyond, ensuring the interests of each child’s future were of paramount importance. They have shown me what difference an exceptional school with phenomenal staff members can do for students, hence why I decided to become a teacher myself.
Commonly parents have an idea of what they’d like to see within the school to better their children’s school experience but often have no way of addressing them. Hence why I chose to become a parent governor as it gave me the opportunity to see what decisions are and will be made, enabling me to communicate some of the concerns and ideas parents would like to put forward to the governing board and collectively work together to create a safe space for our children to get the best out of their education.
Parent Governor Term of office ends June 2026
Joining the school governor team has greatly influenced me personally and given me the chance to participate more in school’s educational activities by using my transferable skills, knowledge, and experience to support the academic work and governance, making sure that both students and teachers—teaching and non-teaching—were valued and entitled to the fundamental resources and standards of good education, and taking good care of the school environment for everyone’s mental health.
It has given me an opportunity to observe student progress throughout the school via the team, with a focus on contributing to the curriculum, monitoring various aspects of the work being done and providing support in any possible way I can, and promoting the wellbeing of the school employees.
I’ve always had a passion for helping and caring for people, therefore it is a wonderful honour for me to be a part of the team that monitors the school’s performance, assists students and staff in realising their full potential, and ensures that standards are recognised.

Originally from Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, I qualified as a PE teacher and Sports Scientist in 2002. Later, I moved to London in 2008 to pursue a Master’s degree which opened up a new path, ultimately leading to a career in finance and accounting.
In 2018, when my daughter was born, I moved to the area and was really blessed to live really close to such an amazing school which she also loves and enjoy. I currently work as a service accountant in a local authority where I developed a great knowledge of school’s funding including DfE grants and SEN Funding.
I believe in the transformative power of education as a key driver of social mobility. Quality, universal education is a fundamental human right that every child should enjoy in order to become a critical, engaged citizen and contribute to building a better society.
I am extremely proud to be a parent governor at Middle Park and hope to be able to offer constructive challenge and support to help the school achieve its educational goals.
Staff Elected Governor
It is always a privilege to be part of the Middle Park community and being a staff governor has allowed me the opportunity to develop this even further.
As a parent of two lovely children, I understand what it is like to have your children walk through the school gates in the morning and recognise the trust families put into schools to look after and educate their children. I have seen how my own children have flourished in a caring and engaging school environment and believe that every child has the right to thrive in a safe and nurturing school community.
Having taught for over twenty years, in schools in both Bexley and Greenwich, I have grown a deep understanding of the teaching and learning process and bring this experience to my governor role. I have led several subjects and phases across the schools allowing me to bring an authentic voice to school discussions. My experience within developing the school curriculum at Middle Park will also allow me to help our governing body have a sound understanding of our school and the learning within it.

pageCache.text:
Music
At Middle Park we value music and the enjoyment it creates. Through our teaching we aim to include a diverse variety of music genres and link our teaching to many places around the world. Music is a uniquely human form of expression. We are aiming to inspire and create learners who have an understanding and appreciation of music. We want all children to develop their confidence and understanding with composition and performance to create well rounded musicians in all areas of music.
We follow an exciting music scheme called Charanga. As children progress through the curriculum, they have the opportunity to listen, compose, improvise, rehearse and perform. We aim to embed a love of music and free expression in all our children as we know this will enrich their whole education.
There are many opportunities for singing and performing together and this helps children develop a sense of unity. They join together to sing in assemblies and perform to audiences at events throughout the year.
In Key Stage 2 some children have been offered the opportunity to have additional small group tuition with a music tutor. Children are able to become proficient in playing either the guitar or trumpet and build on and develop their skills each year.
